editorial:
Imagine a guy who thinks he is the king of the streets but has no clue how the real world works. That is Ali G, and he is dropped right into the middle of the British government. You get to watch this loud, tracksuit-wearing character ask the most ridiculous questions to serious politicians who do not know how to handle him. The whole vibe is just chaotic fun. It feels like a giant prank that goes way too far, and the best part is seeing the high-society types get completely confused by his slang and weird logic.

Sacha Baron Cohen is a genius here because he never breaks character, which makes the funny moments hit harder. The pacing is quick, though some of the political side-plots might feel a bit slow compared to the jokes. If you like awkward humor and seeing powerful people look silly, you will love this. You should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best experience, or you can just rent it on Apple TV for a movie night with friends. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is also a great move if you want to rewatch the best gags.
endingExplained: In the end, the evil Chancellor tries to use Ali G to destroy the Prime Minister, but it totally backfires. Ali G accidentally makes the government look cool to young people, which actually helps the Prime Minister stay in power. The Chancellor gets exposed and fails in his plan to take over. Everything wraps up with Ali G remaining as clueless as ever, proving that being yourself, even if you are weird, can accidentally change the world.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cringe humor and political pranks.
